angle: WR/TE route-cut mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G: decel into the break, speed through it, re-acceleration out), graded by the same code on the same NFL route families (slant, out, hitch, in, corner) and tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out draft classes; last season's SOE as a day-3 override rule; 2026 GO/HOLD calls.
metric_name: Break G: mean tracked acceleration (g, push as a share of body weight) over the second around the slowest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year, reliability-shrunk; 1 sd = 0.021 g.
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [90%: -3.6, +1.0], n=116 receivers in unseen classes; TOST p at +/-3 in = 0.10 (benefit excluded, equivalence not shown). Day-3 override of the draft slot by last-season SOE (WR, any pick gap): 19 overrides, wrong 37 per 100 [21, 56] vs break-even 67, net +7.4 in of next-season SOE per override [-2.9, +18.1]; pre-registered day-3 gain 0.31 [-0.08, 0.63], receiver-clustered shuffle p 0.12.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_18/revised applying the round-18 top_changes. Title as suggested; lede in inches only (Break G slope and net SOE per override). Break G definition opens with one coach-repeatable sentence; physics derivation removed. New Table 1 puts all reliabilities in one place (40 -> NFL top speed 0.43, split-half 0.28, test-retest ICC 0.05, one rep -> second rep 0.53 -> 0.62, drill -> NFL 0.02, SOE 60% signal). 'What to do' split into five items; the day-3 rule stated once with one confidence label. Data science: formal bootstrap TOST for Break G and each mechanic (Break G p 0.10; mechanics about 0.2 to 0.4); override rule as a decision table by pick gap (<16, <32 pre-set, any) with overrides, Jeffreys interval on the wrong rate, break-even, cost of a wrong override in inches and catches, and net SOE per override with receiver-clustered interval, on wide receivers only; GO/HOLD rule written down and back-tested leave-one-season-out on the 2023 and 2024 lists against a pick-only list of the same size (3 of 5 vs 3 of 5, reported as inconclusive); sensitivity grid (sensitivity.csv: shrinkage off/half/double, 5/8/12 NFL breaks, 50/100/150 routes, 100/200 career routes); robustness checks moved to robustness.csv; verify.py rebuilds SOE from raw NGS separation. Football: 2026 list extended to six WR (3 GO incl. Troy Franklin, 3 HOLD incl. Isaiah Bond) with drop-off points (2026 SOE over the first 150 routes that pulls true SOE below zero) and man/zone, slot/wide splits with cell n in the table; 'what flips each name' paragraph; null-in-names table cut to six wide receivers (no TE). Viz: Fig 2A dropped, speed benchmark folded into Fig 1A; Fig 2 is the equivalence forest with slope, TOST p and reliability columns; Fig 3 is small multiples of the six 2026 names with drill rep, median NFL snap and league-median ghost path, entry speed and Break G printed; Fig 4B relabelled as the override rule against break-even with cost of a wrong call; Fig 5 HOLD in orange squares, drop-off markers, decision date in the title; all text 10.5 pt or larger.
open_risks: The day-3 evidence is still unproven: gain p 0.12, net SOE per override interval crosses zero (-2.9 to +18.1), 19 overrides share 11 receivers, and the 50+ route sensitivity variant drops the gain to 0.11.
The GO/HOLD back-test has only 5 act-on names (3 hits) and ties the pick-only list; it cannot support the calls on its own.
Equivalence at +/-3 in is not shown (TOST p 0.10); harm down to -3.6 in per sd is not excluded.
Fig 3, the splits and the drill-to-NFL link rest on sampled NFL plays (up to 40 per player, half top-EPA); the protocol change (cap entry speed, add reps) is inferred, not tested.
Troy Franklin is GO by rule although his true-SOE interval spans zero (+3.4 [-4.0, +10.9]); judges may read that as a rule artefact.
